card: Enables the -Wextra-semi compiler warning flag in CMake and removes redundant semicolons across 66 files in the codebase. It improves compiler hygiene and prevents future stray semicolons from being introduced. Importance is minimal as it is purely internal code styling and compiler warning enforcement. The PR contains a temporary nomerge commit waiting for an upstream libmultiprocess subtree update.
changed_since_previous: Rebased without substantive changes to the approach or commit structure.
evidence: PR description: 'Enable -Wextra-semi and delete all the redundant semicolons.'
problem: Extraneous semicolons throughout C++ headers and source files violate style hygiene and trigger compiler warnings under `-Wextra-semi`, preventing that warning from being enabled to catch redundant semicolons systematically.

risk.why: Mistakes are confined to build flags and purely cosmetic syntax removals with no effect on runtime behavior.

scope_notes: Touches over 60 files across the codebase in a mechanical manner. Includes a temporary `[nomerge]` commit modifying `src/ipc/libmultiprocess` files that is pending an upstream libmultiprocess subtree pull.
summary: Enables the `-Wextra-semi` compiler warning flag in CMake and removes redundant semicolons after method definitions, namespaces, and declarations across the codebase. It also adjusts the disabled fallback definition of `TRACEPOINT_SEMAPHORE` in `src/util/trace.h` to expand to a forward struct declaration so trailing semicolons at macro call sites remain syntactically valid.
